question: Spain breaches the principle of sincere cooperation by regularising 500 000 irregular migrants

The European Commission recently presented a five-year strategy on migration and asylum, at the heart of which is new common system for the return of third-country nationals who do not have a right to legal stay or asylum in the European Union. Meanwhile, Spain has suddenly adopted a policy advocating mass regularisation of irregular migrants, who may have entered the country just five months ago.

This choice violates the principle of sincere cooperation laid down in Article 4 TEU and is not in line with the common European priority that was set to bolster joint Europe-wide returns to non-EU countries. What is more, the initiative in question may create a distortion and problems in the Schengen area, as it may give rise to uncontrolled movements within Member States.

Finally, it actually sends out a message of hope that mass regularisations could happen at any moment, thus encouraging new migration flows. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

How does it assess this breach of the principle of sincere cooperation and its incompatibility with the objectives and principles of the new five-year EU strategy on migration and asylum, in particular with regard to return policies?
What critical coordination tools is it proposing or already using to ensure that the objective of increasing the rate of returns of irregular migrants is achieved?
What further measures can it take to ensure the proper functioning of the Schengen area?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.5.2026) Notwithstanding the distribution of competences defined by the EU legal order in relation to policies and individual decisions to regularise the status of illegally staying third-country nationals, in an area without internal borders, Member States’ decisions may have consequences on other Member States and on the EU as a whole.

A national residence permit issued by a Member State does not give authorisation to settle freely around the EU, but only to live and work in the Member State that issued it1. If a permit holder is found illegally staying or applies for asylum in another Member State, the permit holder must return to the issuing Member State.

National authorities must act in a spirit of sincere cooperation for this to happen swiftly. The Commission is advancing a new EU common approach to returns. The proposed Return Regulation2, which is currently under negotiation, aims to provide Member States with a more efficient framework to increase returns.

Work is ongoing on the digitalisation of return, readmission and reintegration, with a proposal planned in 2026. The forthcoming revision of the Regulation on the European Border and Coast Guard Agency3 will also provide an opportunity to strengthen its role in returns. The Commission monitors the application of EU law in all Member States, including through the Schengen Evaluation Monitoring Mechanism4.
This is without prejudice to the possibility of using other instruments at its disposal as guardian of the Treaties.
1 Article 21 of the Convention implementing the Schengen Agreement of 14 June 1985 between the

Governments of the States of the Benelux Economic Union, the Federal Republic of Germany and the French Republic on the gradual abolition of checks at their common borders, OJ L 239, 22.09.2000, pp 19-62: ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/convention/2000/922/oj.

2 Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing a common system for the return of third-country nationals staying illegally in the Union, and repealing Directive 2008/115/EC of the European Parliament and the Council, Council Directive 2001/40/EC and Council Decision 2004/191/EC.

3 Regulation (EU) 2019/1896 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 November 2019 on the European Border and Coast Guard and repealing Regulations (EU) No 1052/2013 and (EU) 2016/1624, OJ L 295, 14.11.2019, pp. 1–131.

4 Council Regulation (EU) 2022/922 of 9 June 2022 on the establishment and operation of an evaluation and monitoring mechanism to verify the application of the Schengen acquis, and repealing Regulation (EU) No 1053/2013.
